## Summary

A recommendation of Harvard's **CS2680 "Modern AI Systems"**, framed by the observation that top universities teaching agents now go all the way down to the GPU. The course arc: starts at **Claude Code, agent loops, evals, and token cost**, then descends the systems stack through **model deployment, routing, KV cache, quantization, and speculative decoding**. The assignment design is singled out as clever — 5 assignments all built around the same agent (claim truncated at capture).

## Why it matters

- **The curricular claim is the signal.** A Harvard course that treats Claude Code / agent loops as the motivating application and teaches inference economics (token cost, KV cache, quantization) as core syllabus material marks where practical AI engineering is consolidating: agents as the entry point, the full serving stack as the prerequisite. That's a useful map of what "modern AI systems" competence now includes.
- **Direct overlap with our own stack decisions.** Token cost, routing, and evals are exactly the levers in our agent operations (compute caps, model routing, capture-quality checks). The public course materials could serve as a free, structured reference for those topics rather than ad-hoc blog posts.
- **Skepticism gates:** single enthusiast's recommendation, no personal outcome claimed; tweet truncated mid-assignment-description so the "5 assignments, one agent" design claim is unverifiable from the capture; course site/materials unverified as of capture (may be login-gated or partially public); 95 replies unread — possible pushback or corrections not examined.
